title: Queue priming & shadow-gate sync notes - Oct 28 2026
body:
Purpose: capture the sync from 2026-10-28 covering recent benchmark runs that surfaced p95/p99 latency regressions during short, high-arrival bursts. This doc is a working artifact — hypothesis-led notes, quick data excerpts, and concrete next steps to unblock the shadow/gating plan.

Agenda:
- Quick recap of the regression window (10/26-10/27 smoke runs)
- Reproduce steps and test harness config used in the runs
- Observed signals and anomaly signatures (time series snippets)
- Root-cause hypotheses and quick experiments to validate
- Shadow-gate rollout adjustments and acceptance criteria
- Action items and owners

Recap / context:
- Regression first seen in CI smoke and then reproducible in the lab when running mixed-sequence workloads with variable arrival jitter. Affected model: open-metric-7B-v2 (same variant used in canary).
- Baseline SLO: p95 <= 100 ms for short sequences (<= 128 tokens), p99 <= 220 ms. During bursts, p95 climbed to 350–480 ms and p99 spiked to >900 ms for short windows (~30–90s).
- Reproducible with both jambench harness and in-cluster shadow traffic replay. Shadow-gate (traffic-limited) showed reduced but still visible latency bumps.

Test harness configuration (how we reproduced):
- jambench config: qps target 120, mix: 60% seq32 / 30% seq128 / 10% seq512, arrival jitter: exp(0.3) to mimic front-end bunched arrivals.
- Cluster test: 8-nodes x gtx-pool3, autoscaler disabled, KV-cache warm state (hit rate ~72% before runs).
- Batcher settings: dynamic-batcher enabled; batch_size_cap=128 tokens; batching-window-ms=12ms; prefer-fast-path=true.
- Shadow gating: gating fraction = 0.15 (15% of production traffic), fallback to smaller model variant if latency > 400ms for >10s.

Key observations / signals:
- Queue fill snapshots (sampled every 50ms) show short-lived peaks where instantaneous queued tokens jump 2–6x for 200–800ms. Those peaks align exactly with p95 spikes.
- Batch size distribution shifts during peaks: median batch tokens moves from 24 -> 110, causing larger kernel launches and longer individual token latencies.
- KV cache hit-rate dips by ~8–12% during the same windows (prefix cache thrash suspected).
- Sidecar probe (heap/metrics) shows small native allocator stalls on 2 nodes coincident with spikes; not full GC but allocation backpressure observed in C++ sidecar logs.
- Observability traces: long tail is dominated by model-infer time when big microbatches are processed; scheduling delay (time request waits as part of a batch) accounts for 60–75% of added latency during incidents.

Immediate hypotheses (ranked):
1) Batching heuristic amplification: arrival jitter + current batching-window leads to sudden coalescing of very large batches for short windows; runtime kernel selection isn't optimal for those large microbatches causing heavy tail.
2) KV cache pressure & eviction storm: simultaneous popularity shift for a small set of prefixes causes cache thrash and increases decode time (more attention state misses).
3) Sidecar allocator/backpressure: temporary memory allocator contention increases time-to-schedule for worker threads on affected nodes.
4) Smart-routing feedback loop: when a zone becomes slightly slower, a routing tweak retries or re-routes causing short bursts to a smaller subset of nodes amplifying burstiness.

Quick experiments run during the sync:
- Lowered batching-window-ms from 12 -> 6 on a 2-node test subset: p95 reduced ~28% during synthetic bursts, batch size distribution capped (median remained <60 tokens).
- Reduced batch_size_cap from 128 -> 64: p99 tail decreased but end-to-end throughput lost ~9% in steady-state; acceptable for canary if limited to bursty routes only.
- Increased prefix-cache TTL to 60s in lab: observed hit-rate increase ~6% and p95 improved marginally (~10%); suggests cache warming helps but not the dominant factor.
- Injected 150ms arrival jitter smoothing at client-simulator: latency spikes largely dissipated — indicates front-end pacing is a strong mitigant but not always possible in prod.

Shadow-gate rollout plan discussion:
- Current shadow gating approach rejects >X% of shadow traffic when latency > threshold and falls back to smaller model. That helps availability but masks the underlying regression. We need a two-pronged approach: (A) gate-by-route (only apply gating to high-variance routes) and (B) adaptive-batch caps during detected microburst windows.
- Acceptance criteria for opening shadow gate wider: sustained p95 <= 140ms across 24h of mixed traffic and no p99 spikes > 350ms lasting >2 minutes.

Proposed immediate mitigations (do-first list):
1) Short-term: Roll batch_size_cap=64 for routes tagged bursty (route metadata: /chat/stream, /completion/parity) — roll this via feature-flag for 48h. Owner: Gregory Park. Due: 2026-10-30.
2) Add heuristic: if instantaneous queued tokens > 4x median for route over 1s, temporarily halve batching-window-ms for that route (adaptive windowing). Owner: Lina Kowalski. Prototype by 2026-11-02.
3) Expose queue_fill_snapshot metric (histogram of queued tokens per sample) and a derived alert if >90th percentile > threshold. Owner: Nikhil Rao. JIRA: JIRA-INF-4892. Due: 2026-10-31.
4) Prevent cache eviction storms: bump prefix cache TTL to 60s for candidate routes and monitor hit-rate. Owner: Ethan Rivera. Run 72h experiment starting 2026-10-29.
5) Experiment: add a client-side micro-pacer for 10% of traffic to validate smoothing at scale. Owner: Sofia Alvarez. Start 2026-11-01.

Longer-term engineering changes (backlog candidates):
- Revisit batcher kernel-selection: add a fast-path for medium-large batches (64–128 tokens) that currently falls back to generic kernel. Estimated effort: 2 sprints.
- Improve sidecar allocator behavior to avoid allocation stalls at high burst rates; profile and consider jemalloc tuning or arena preallocation.
- Routing policy: add burst-aware routing that spreads microbursts across more nodes rather than concentrating.

Acceptance metrics we will observe during the next 72h:
- p95 for short sequences <= 140ms (target)
- p99 <= 350ms, and no >2 minute continuous window above that during synthetic jittered runs
- Queue_fill_snapshot 95th percentile < 1.8x baseline during traffic runs
- KV-cache hit-rate not drop >5% from baseline during bursts

Open questions / risks:
- Will halving batch_size_cap be too expensive for high-throughput steady-state routes? Need to run cost vs latency tradeoff analysis after 48h trial.
- Adaptive windowing complexity: risk of oscillation if multiple nodes simultaneously toggle windows; need damping/backoff.
- Shadow gating currently hides incidents; we must ensure observability remains robust so we don't regress silently when gating is enabled.

Action items (explicit):
- Gregory Park: Feature-flag rollout batch_size_cap=64 for tagged routes, run 48h. Deliverable: rollout plan + rollback steps. Due 2026-10-30.
- Lina Kowalski: Prototype adaptive batching-window heuristic (server-side) and a simple param-store flag to enable. Due 2026-11-02.
- Nikhil Rao: Implement queue_fill_snapshot metric + grafana dashboard panel + alert. JIRA-INF-4892. Due 2026-10-31.
- Ethan Rivera: Launch prefix cache TTL experiment (60s) for candidate routes; collect hit-rate and latency deltas for 72h. Due 2026-11-02.
- Sofia Alvarez: Coordinate client-side pacer A/B (10% traffic) and run smoke for 48h. Deliver results summary. Due 2026-11-03.
- Avery Chen: Open PR with a short readme describing the incident patterns and link to this doc; include reproduction steps and test harness configs. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1327. Due 2026-10-29.

Notes / logs attached:
- Sample trace ids: trace-20261027-8a7f, trace-20261027-9b2c, trace-20261028-1c3e (use these to drill into p95 spike windows).
- Lab run ids: lab-run-2026-10-27-burst-a, lab-run-2026-10-28-shadow-pass-1.

Next sync: 2026-11-02 10:00 PT — focus on results from the 48/72h experiments and decide whether to widen routing or revert changes.

Notes to self (informal):
- This doc will become the canonical handoff for SRE/observability to add the metric and alert. Keep it terse but include reproduction commands in the PR.
- Try to capture before/after histograms and place them in Confluence page linked above.

Summary: We have a reproducible microburst-induced p95/p99 regression dominated by batching amplification and temporary cache/allocator pressure. Short-term mitigations (batch caps + pacing + cache TTL bump) look promising; the primary engineering work is an adaptive batcher/window heuristic and improved kernel-selection for medium-large batches.
